theorem.quantifiers: Every prime p, every finite p-basis field K of characteristic p, every derivative-stable coefficient subring A contained in an arbitrary subring R of K, every finite family of ordinary derivative words, and every rational scalar s in K.
hypotheses: The p-basis monomials span K over p-th powers, the coordinate derivations have their prescribed coordinate values, and the additive Cartier map extracts the top p-basis coefficient.
A is closed under the coordinate derivatives; c_j belongs to A; g and t_j belong to R.
psi is an additive map R to R and its inclusion into K equals Cartier(s*r) for every r in R.
theorem.explicit_witness: T=sum_j t_j adjoint_word_j(c_j), with each derivative transferred onto the coefficient with a minus sign and reversed order.
theorem.conclusion: T belongs to R and psi(g*T)=psi(1). For every ideal I not containing psi(1), psi(gR) is not contained in I.
not_assumed: R is normal, regular, complete, or unramified
the normalization or branch degree is less than p
proved_not_assumed: Cartier annihilates every coordinate derivative on the entire p-basis field.
Integration by parts for every finite derivative word.
The adjoint coefficient remains in A.
The explicit witness gives exactly psi(1), not just an unspecified nonzero image.

jacobian.mathematical_scope: A single QQ coefficient derivative, not a Cartier-field or completion solver and not proof of the theorem.

supplemental_experiments.description: Deterministic exact Laurent-polynomial checks, complementary Cartier extraction, and tame ramified trace checks. These are diagnostics, not the parameter-uniform proof.
supplemental_experiments.tame_trace_exponent_range: For each tested p and 2 <= e < p, all integer exponents from -2*p*e through 2*p*e.
hypothesis_controls: For every prime p, s=u^(p-1), g=u^p and psi(r)=Cartier(s*r) give psi(1)=1 and psi(gR) contained in (u).
The nonregular order-zero coefficient u^(-p) produces a scalar identity but violates coefficient regularity.
The p-th Hasse derivative produces a scalar identity because binomial(2*p-1,p)=1 modulo p, but it is not an allowed ordinary derivative of retained order below p.

application.regular_at: Every closed point b of each specified retained chart
geometric_inputs_not_formalized: The characteristic-zero differential identity and its retained reduction
